The new American retirement plan equates to working forever: Nonexistent nest eggs and most Americans are bad at planning as to how long they will live.

Some thoughts - Our society is so broken on the matter of care of elderly (or retired if you like that word better) it's shocking. "Retirement" was an idea concocted to fund the markets and give Americans some small sliver of life without needing 9-5 work. Americans haven't only done poor planning, that's blaming the victims in part - there is a war on savers and those that have been prudent have seen their savings gutted by ZIRP. There's no solution to this as the labor market has done away with many benefits, such as pension plans, defined benefit plans, etc.

Allowing people to die when they choose might help the distress of those who find themselves destitute in old age. Families caring for their own elderly would help but with everybody working to pay the bills, who cares for the old ones? Even if you have $, you will work until you die. Cooking, cleaning, home repair, caring for family - there will be work of some kind until one dies. This "work" is simply uncompensated and under valued in our country.

For the benefit of readers here I would like to take a quick look generally at the two types of 'plans.'

Defined Benefit Plans provide a string of guaranteed payments to a retired person on a regular periodic basis for the rest of the persons life. These are often referred to as 'traditional pensions.' Whatever the exact financial situation of the person, one thing is for sure: that check will always be there, typically every month as long as the person lives.

Defined Contribution Plans are the other kind of 'retirement.' Really, this is not retirement at all but a pile of money set aside under a temporary tax preference. This pile of money is entirely disconnected with the lifespan of the individual. If the person outlives the fund, the annuity stops coming. If the person dies early, the money goes into the estate.

What % of American's have these anymore? Not many according to the article. What if you are retiring during the next big market crash and your account value decreases by 50-75%? Too bad so sad. All these rigged games to get Americans to put their retirement into the markets are just that - rigged games.

Very good points. I just wanted to cover the basics. Now, to the discussion!

Defined Contribution Plans are essentially a multi-generational pyramid scheme. Massive amounts of money flood into the stock market in the 80's as a result of deregulation, IRAs and the like. The flood continues in the 90's as government plans including TSP proliferate. All this money coming in inflates the stock market literally for decades until we reach saturation point. Then, the big gains stop.

The above-average gains in the stock market in recent years are a direct result of flooding it with these tax preferred schemes. The only other thing contributing to these gains are rapid productivity gains. We can argue over how much goes to which. Interestingly, increased productivity will eventually reduce the availability of these funds, as automation places people out of work and forces downward pressure on wages.
